body:

Dedupe keywords: `ComponentPropsMap`, `object-map map describe`, `locationField optional`, `NavigationModeSchema new_window`, `objectui-pin-citations historical spelling`.

## Why this exists: carried BEFORE its PR was enqueued, so the landing settles nothing it did not

PR #18403 passed at-tier contract review at head `c431c22e05` (record `5697057114`, **VERDICT: PASS**). That review named **four** non-blocking imprecisions and said the seat may fold them into the next round touching those lines. ⭐ Two of them **ship into the public reference** (`content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx`), so they are recorded here rather than left in a review comment.

⚠️ The seat notes plainly: the reviewer judged these non-blocking and the seat adopted its verdict **verbatim**, as the protocol requires. ⛔ This card is not an appeal of that verdict. It is the carrier for what the verdict explicitly left open.

## N1 — ships. The `object-map` `map` describe overstates what is required

The describe writes `{ latitudeField, longitudeField, locationField?, … }`, marking the lat/lng **pair required**.

Measured at the objectui pin `53ded82b`: `ObjectMapConfigSchema` declares **all eight keys `.optional()`**, and the renderer's flat branch (`ObjectMap.tsx:382`) accepts `locationField` **alone**. The spec's own `ListMapConfigSchema` describes `locationField` as the alternative to the pair.

⇒ an author reading the shipped reference is told to supply two keys when one suffices. The error is **conservative** — they would write more than needed, nothing is refused (the door is `z.unknown()`) — which is why it is not blocking. It is still a false statement about the accept set, in text that generates public documentation.

Suggested spelling: `latitudeField?, longitudeField?`, or "either `locationField` or the `latitudeField`/`longitudeField` pair".

## N2 — ships. The navigation mode list omits `new_window`

Three navigation rows list `page | drawer | modal | split | popover | none`. The spec's `NavigationModeSchema` declares **seven** values including `new_window`, and objectui's `useNavigationOverlay.ts` switches on it at the pin (`:298`, 5 hits).

⚠️ Inherited, not introduced: the existing object-grid row lists **five** of the seven (no `popover`, no `new_window`), so this PR's list is **closer** to complete than the precedent it copied. Fixing it means fixing the family, not just these three rows.

## N3 — source only, never generated

`component.test.ts` carries two comment citations that were not carried when the zod headers were corrected: `:3425` reads `label (:1849)` where the read is `:1871`; `:3521` reads "`ObjectGantt.tsx:501` validates" where the safeParse is `:500`. Same class as the F3 items that round fixed in the schema headers.

## N4 — gate coverage, not text truth

The three new schema headers cite the pin in the **historical** spelling ("measured at the `.objectui-sha` pin `53ded82b`") while the sibling #7751 rows use the **asserting** spelling (`.objectui-sha` = `53ded82bf`, 7 sites). `check:objectui-pin-citations` therefore counts these ~45 line anchors among its "36 historical not checked" and **will not flag them on the next pin bump**. The gate permits the historical form, so nothing is violated — but ~45 anchors that exist to stay re-checkable are, in practice, not being checked.
